{{Quote|Behold the patron of glory! Eyes afire with righteous might; skin bathed in the warm blood of the enemy&mdash;witness the glory and blazing fury!<br />His wrath rains down like fire from above. Bodies encircle him like a pyre. His hand never falters; his courage never wanes as the hordes overwhelm him.<br />His last thoughts turn to his true love. He feels no fear. No pain. The chill of death cannot cool his passion. The hero burns eternal.|Tala-Reh recites part of the poem|<ref name="Vault" />}}
A '''poem''' was composed by the [[Voss (species)|Voss]] [[Species/Legends|species]] in their native [[Voss (language)|language]] that celebrated a [[Voss commandos|Voss commando]] after his [[Death/Legends|death]] at the hands of [[Jokull]], the king of the hostile [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]] species, on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Voss]]. The [[Tala-Reh's husband|husband]] of fellow commando [[Tala-Reh]], the commando had gone to his [[Death/Legends|death]] at the request of the [[Voss Mystics|Mystic]] [[Valen-Da]] and killed twenty Gormak warriors before he himself was slain, and his wife favored the poem above the other hymns and songs written in his honor after the man's demise. She recited it to the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Hero of Tython]] while working with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], as the Knight reminded her of her husband despite being an outsider.<ref name="Vault" />

==Behind the scenes==
The poem first appeared in the Jedi Knight class mission "Vault of the Gormak King" in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] in [[2011]]. Tala-Reh recites the first verse, and she will complete the rest of the poem if the player allows her to.<ref name="Vault" />
